# QS-CFW-5349-60 Quality specification - track link CFW-5349-60 (15B37)

Revision: Rev B  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-5349-60

## Scope
This quality specification defines acceptance criteria and inspection methods for the manufactured track link CFW-5349-60 (CFW-5349-60) produced at Plant P1. It applies to forged parts delivered to assembly, parts returned from heat treatment, and finished parts submitted for final inspection. The document covers material condition, dimensional control of the bore, hardness acceptance, inspection procedures, sampling rationale, and controls for nonconforming items. This specification is intended for use by production, quality, and metallurgical personnel.

## Requirements table
| Characteristic | Requirement | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Material hardness | 31-35 HRC | Hardness applies to working surface and cross section representative of the bore area. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | ±0.03 mm | Applies after final machining and before assembly processes. Measurement method is described below. |
| Maximum forging weight | 58.0 kg | Maximum weight per individual forged blank prior to machining. Exceeding items are processed as nonconforming. |

Rationale: The hardness band is selected to ensure adequate wear resistance while maintaining toughness for the dynamic loading environment of the track link. The bore tolerance is dictated by mating component fit and lubrication retention requirements. The maximum forging weight reflects handling and die capacity constraints at Plant P1.

## Inspection method
General approach
- Inspectors shall verify each characteristic in the Requirements table prior to release to the next operation. Records must document the inspector identity, inspection equipment used, and results observed.
- Calibration status of all measuring equipment shall be verified against the calibration control system prior to use. Use equipment with appropriate resolution and repeatability for the characteristic measured.

Hardness verification
- Hardness shall be measured on a minimum of one location representative of the bore region on every finished part. If part geometry prevents direct indentation in the bore, an adjacent location that has undergone identical heat treatment and machining shall be used. When a part is measured, record the instrument identifier and reading. Acceptance is granted only when the measured value falls within 31-35 HRC.
- If a measured value is outside the specified range, follow the nonconformance handling section below.

Bore diameter measurement
- Measure the bore diameter after final machining using a bore gauge or coordinate measuring system capable of resolving the specified tolerance. Record the nominal dimension and deviation. Acceptance requires the measured diameter to be within ±0.03 mm of the specified nominal bore dimension as provided on the drawing for part CFW-5349-60.
- For runs with multiple pieces, apply a sampling rationale consistent with Plant P1 sampling procedures. If any sampled piece exceeds the tolerance, expand inspection to the entire lot and hold the lot pending disposition.

Forging weight control
- Weigh every forged blank prior to machining and confirm it does not exceed 58.0 kg. Weighing shall be performed on calibrated scales. If a blank exceeds the maximum, segregate and label it as a potential nonconforming blank and notify production supervision for evaluation.

Surface and visual checks
- Perform a visual inspection to detect forging defects, cracks, excessive laps, or surface contamination that could affect subsequent machining or performance. Any visual anomalies that may compromise fit, function, or fatigue life shall be recorded and processed under nonconformance handling.

Records to keep
- For each batch, retain an inspection record that includes: part identifier, serial or lot identifier, inspector initials, caliper or instrument identifiers, hardness readings, bore measurement results, forging weight records, visual inspection notes, and disposition decisions. Maintain these records in the document control system and on the shop floor for traceability.
- Keep hardness test block comparisons used to verify hardness tester performance with the inspection data for that shift.

Examples
- Example of acceptable condition: A finished link with a recorded hardness of thirty-two point five HRC within the range 31-35 HRC, bore measurements recorded within ±0.03 mm relative to nominal, and forging weight recorded below 58.0 kg is acceptable for release.
- Example of reject condition: A forged blank measured at a weight exceeding 58.0 kg, or a machined part with a bore outside ±0.03 mm, or a hardness reading outside 31-35 HRC, is subject to the nonconformance process and may require rework, segregation, or scrap.

## Nonconformance handling
Segregation and hold
- Any item that fails to meet the Requirements table shall be immediately segregated and labeled as nonconforming. Do not release nonconforming items to downstream operations without documented disposition.

Disposition options
- Rework: If the deviation is something that can be corrected by defined machining or heat treatment processes without compromising part integrity, a controlled rework plan may be approved by quality engineering. Reworked parts must be re-inspected to demonstrate compliance with the Requirements table.
- Use-as-is: Rare dispositions for use-as-is must be supported by engineering analysis demonstrating that functional performance is not compromised and must be approved by authorized engineering personnel. The basis for approval must be documented and retained.
- Scrap: Parts that cannot be reworked or approved for use-as-is shall be scrapped and recorded.

Investigation and corrective action
- For any recurring nonconformance, initiate a root cause investigation. Document findings, corrective actions, and verification steps. Implement corrective action to prevent recurrence and verify effectiveness through subsequent inspection results.

Notifications and records
- Notify production supervision and quality management of any nonconformance that affects delivery or safety. Maintain records of nonconformance forms, dispositions, investigation reports, and corrective action records in the document control and quality management systems.

Audit and review
- Quality shall periodically review inspection records to confirm continued conformance to this specification and to identify any trends. Findings and corrective actions shall be recorded and retained as part of the plant quality records.

End of specification.
